standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the four equivalences of the statement to the single algebraic property.

standard_prerequisites.name: The same-chapter characterization of quasi-finiteness at a point by the corresponding property of the local ring map
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the morphism-level property with the ring-level property P, completing the reduction.

standard_prerequisites.name: That being of finite type is already known to be a local property of ring maps, together with the fact that quasi-finiteness at a prime depends only on the local ring
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies conditions (a) and (b) for quasi-finiteness and the local-ring reduction used in condition (c).

core_obligations: Define the property P of a ring map to mean that the map is quasi-finite, and claim that P is a local property of ring maps in the sense of the cited definition (proof lines 4078-4081).

Verify conditions (a), (b) and (c): for finite type maps quasi-finiteness at a prime depends only on the local ring, so the known locality of finite type, together with the localization of the local ring at a standard open, gives all three conditions; the author spells out the argument for a family of localizations generating the unit ideal (proof lines 4082-4100).

Apply the same-chapter result on local properties to conclude that it suffices to show that local quasi-finiteness of f is equivalent to f being locally of type P, and then use the characterization of quasi-finiteness at a point by the local ring map to finish (proof lines 4102-4110).
proof_roadmap: Show that quasi-finiteness is a local property of ring maps by checking the three conditions of the definition (proof lines 4078-4100).
Invoke the local-property machinery and the pointwise characterization of quasi-finiteness to conclude all four equivalences and the final statement about restrictions (proof lines 4102-4110).
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four equivalent ways of saying that a morphism is locally quasi-finite, together with the stability of the property under restriction to open subschemes (statement lines 4055-4076). The counted proof is a reduction rather than a citation: it defines the ring-level property, verifies the three local-property conditions for it by appealing to the fact that quasi-finiteness at a prime depends only on the local ring and by arguing through a cover of the ring by localizations, and then invokes the local-property machinery and the pointwise characterization to conclude (proof lines 4078-4110). It is H2: the argument is a well-structured reduction carried out inside the counted span, with no independent research-level content.
